name: flow-field

frames.best_why: A clear circular vortex is visible around the cursor while the full headline stays readable.

tagline: Fine white streamlines drift across a dark field and swirl around the cursor.
summary: A full-bleed canvas of hundreds of particle trails that flow left to right like wind. Moving the pointer bends the streams around it and sheds small vortices, while a click sends a ripple outward.
appearance: A near-black full-bleed surface covered in fine, faint grey streaks all running roughly left to right. Over the centre sit a small pill, a large white headline and a muted paragraph.
behaviour: The trails drift continuously and part around the cursor, shedding small swirling vortices as it moves; a click pushes a ring of air outward. Off screen or under reduced motion it draws a still field and stops the loop.
demo_content: Pill 'Realtime pipelines', heading 'Data that moves the way you think.', subtext about routing events.
search_phrases: click makes a ripple in particles
use_when: A dark hero or section wants a calm animated field that reacts to the pointer without stealing focus.
avoid_when: The page must stay cheap on mobile or low-power devices; it runs a full canvas loop of hundreds of particles.
customise: Set density, speed and interactivity as props, and pass children to overlay copy on the wind. Colours follow the canvas text colour, so a theme class changes them.
weight_why: Up to 700 particle trails drawn to canvas every animation frame, with a reduced idle rate.

a11y.note: The canvas is aria-hidden and decorative; reduced motion is handled by drawing a still field instead of the loop.

issues: Touch only stirs the wind while a finger is held down, so it is weaker on phones.
The trails are very faint behind large text, so the effect is easy to miss in a still.
polish_why: Detailed flow simulation with a clear cursor response; trails stay deliberately faint.
